title: How John Rush runs 26 apps and $250K/month: presales, co-makers, cross-promo
summary: John Rush explains his repeatable blueprint for launching 20+ products: start from your own pain, get a waitlist and presales, deliver manually, then build with a 50/50 co-maker. He covers marketing via SEO, daily social, directories and cross-promotion between apps, plus AI usage, margins and building in public.

principles.text: Validate before building: 100 waitlist signups, a 90% off presale, 5 sales, then deliver the solution manually before any code.
principles.quote: I launch uh a weight list and I see whether I am able to generate 100 signups. I email them all and I offer them 90% discount on a pre-sale before I build anything. And then if I get five sales, I build the first MVP.

principles.text: Iterate on a manual service first; it is far easier to change a routine than code.
principles.quote: it's easier to iterate when there is no product, when there's no code. It's much easier because I just have to change my own routine and my own service.

principles.text: Recruit a co-maker with a validated idea and split ownership 50/50.
principles.quote: if I pitch them the idea that has past the validation part I have pre-sales done and I have some users it's really easy to convince needs them to join and we share the ownership 50/50.

principles.text: Great marketing is a great product, but start average and use boring channels (SEO, daily social, directories) to get first users.
principles.quote: usually you start with an average product and you have to do the boring marketing methods to bring first users and then use those users to improve your product and make it great.

principles.text: Cross-promote and integrate your apps so users flow across the whole ecosystem; free tools feed premium ones.
principles.quote: I link tools with each other and the other thing that's more interesting is that I integrate tools with each other.

principles.text: Building in public builds a direct audience channel that lets you fix products before shipping, cutting failure from 90% to 10%.
principles.quote: Before building in public, my failure rate was really high. 90% of the things I've done failed. And when I start building in public, it flipped.
